comment: He explained difficult concepts in a manageable way. Tests were definitely challenging but after you understand the core concepts you can usually figure out the answer. This class was amazing to prepare me for my future career in medicine. I learned a lot in the class even though it did require putting time into the course.

Tests were a mix of application-base and recall. Labs were mostly through an online program with one wet lab. Dr. Vaughan gives small curves on exams and is very accommodating and flexible. He gives feedback on assignments and on exams. He provides all the resources that a student needs to succeed (practice Qs, study sheets, ppt notes).

All things considering, he is a fair grader and puts a small curve on tests. However I felt monumentally underprepared for tests which were incredibly hard and I felt we werent given enough time to complete them. His class is VERY lecture heavy to the point I spent several hours a day out of class doing lecture notes.

The class periods were used for pointless case studies and the lecture had to be done outside of class. I spent 4-6 hours each day listening to lectures and doing labs/ assignments and didn't feel as though I gained anything from them. The midterm and final combined are worth 1/2 your grade, the tests are hard and there is not enough time given.
Lots of online assignments, lots of memorization. If thats your thing then good.

Do you like memorizing and memory recall? If so you will do well in this class because you don't have to do any critical thinking at all. Just memorize the boring figures in the textbook and he will give you a B.
He is a little monotonous, but he is an excellent teacher. He delivers clear information and really wants his students to learn and do well.
Speaks in a monotonous tone. Very boring. Puts you to sleep. Hard to stay focused.
